nodes.description: Governance address state variable in ERC20, initialized from tx.origin and used as the sole authorization check for privileged minting.
ERC20 constructor that sets _name, _symbol, _decimals and assigns governance = tx.origin, allowing a phishing proxy to become the governance address.
tx.origin used directly as the governance authority, which is attacker-influenceable via phishing / malicious intermediate contracts.
transferFromAndCall(address fromAddress, uint256 SubstractedValue) public; guarded only by require(msg.sender == governance) before minting new tokens.
Parameter fromAddress of transferFromAndCall, used as the mint recipient.
Parameter SubstractedValue of transferFromAndCall, used as the minted amount.
msg.sender used as the access-control subject in transferFromAndCall; compared against the tx.origin-derived governance address.
Unbounded _mint(fromAddress, SubstractedValue) call inside transferFromAndCall; mints arbitrary tokens to an arbitrary address without cap or role verification.
Internal _mint(address account, uint256 amount) that increases _totalSupply and _balances, invoked by the privileged transferFromAndCall path.
Assignment governance = tx.origin in the constructor; trusts a spoofable origin for a privileged role, enabling access-control takeover.

edges.reason: tx.origin flows directly into the governance authority assignment, making the privileged role spoofable via phishing.
The unsafe tx.origin assignment writes the attacker-influenceable value into the governance state variable.
governance state variable is read by the require(msg.sender == governance) guard in transferFromAndCall, controlling who may mint.
msg.sender is compared against governance in the only authorization check of transferFromAndCall; a phished tx.origin lets msg.sender pass the check.
Because the guard derives from a tx.origin-based authority, the tx.origin untrusted input ultimately gates execution of the minting function.
Once the caller satisfies the governance check, transferFromAndCall executes the unchecked mint operation.
User-supplied fromAddress parameter flows into the mint recipient of the unsafe mint call.
User-supplied SubstractedValue parameter flows into the minted amount of the unsafe mint call.
The unsafe mint operation invokes the internal _mint function to create tokens and update total supply.

normalization_plan.reason: Parameter fromAddress has no independent security semantics; it is only consumed as the recipient argument of the unsafe _mint operation, so it should be merged into that unsafe_operation node.
Parameter SubstractedValue has no independent security semantics; it is only consumed as the amount argument of the unsafe _mint operation, so it should be merged into that unsafe_operation node.
